summary: Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He became a professor at the Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992 and founded the GRIMER research group.
Matteo Bartoli (1873–1946) was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1894–1898) and under Heinrich Hübschmann. He held a post at the University of Turin from around 1907 to 1946.

Matthew B. Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisors Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, alongside traditional studies under Hsing Yun and Huishang.

Matthew Immergut is a scholar of religious studies and sociology who studied under Culadasa. Attested in 2011, he served as Associate Professor of Sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

Matthew King is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett in 2014, and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab and Thupten Champa.

Matthew R. Sayers specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle, later holding a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Osaka City University, the Inter-University Center, the University of Hawaiʻi (MA), and Duke University (PhD), his mentors included Richard M. Jaffe, Helen Baroni, and Michel Mohr.

Matthew T. Kapstein (b. 1949) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at UC Berkeley and Brown University. He has held faculty posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Matthias de Vries (1820–1892) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University (~1838–1843). He held academic posts at the University of Groningen (1849–1853) and Leiden University (1853–1891).

Matthias von Lexer (1830–1892) was a linguist who studied at Graz and Erlangen and under Bopp, Haupt, and Weber. He held professorships at the universities of Freiburg (~1864–1868), Würzburg (from 1868), and Munich (1890).

Matthieu Ricard (b. 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He earned a doctorate at the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob, studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Kangyur Rinpoche, and served as a board member of the Mind and Life Institute.

Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed his PhD at SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski. He has held positions at Mahidol University and the International Buddhist College.

Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna. He served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Chicago, Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins under William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Grammont (1866–1946) was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held an academic post at the University of Montpellier from around 1895 to 1939.
Maurice Jametel (1856–1889) was a scholar in sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École des langues orientales and later taught there from around 1886 to 1889.
Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied under Walpola Rahula and held a post at the University of London from around 1955 to 1979.

Maurice Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar educated at Christ's College and Ridley Hall. He held posts at Ridley Hall, University of Ibadan, Clare College, and King's College London, before serving as Oxford's Regius Professor of Divinity (1970–1991).

Maurine Stuart (1922–1990) was an active figure in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Manitoba and trained under Nadia Boulanger, Soen Nakagawa, Eido Tai Shimano, and Yasutani. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Mauro Maggi is a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", served as a researcher at the University of Hamburg (1990), and held posts at IsMEO and Sapienza University of Rome.
